package_info.package_manager: unknown (macOS malware, likely distributed as a Mach-O binary or DMG installer)
package_info.why_malicious: SpectralBlur is a backdoor attributed to North Korean threat actors, designed to provide remote access and control over infected macOS systems. It enables file upload/download, shell command execution, and configuration updates, which are all behaviors consistent with remote access trojans (RATs) and are not expected in legitimate software.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after execution of the malware binary)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Functionality to upload files from the victim's machine to a remote C2 server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads files from the local filesystem and transmits them to a remote command-and-control (C2) server over the network, enabling exfiltration of sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited file exfiltration to an external server is a hallmark of backdoor and RAT malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate macOS applications do not silently upload arbitrary files to remote servers without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Cloud backup or file synchronization tools may upload files, but only with explicit user configuration and consent.
key_indicators: File upload functionality to remote C2
No user interaction or consent required

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after execution of the malware binary)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Functionality to execute arbitrary shell commands received from the C2 server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code receives shell commands from the C2 server and executes them on the infected system, allowing the attacker to perform arbitrary actions remotely.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote shell execution is a primary capability of backdoors and is rarely, if ever, present in legitimate software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not accept and execute remote shell commands from unknown servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools in enterprise environments, but only with strong authentication and user awareness.
key_indicators: Network communication with C2 for command retrieval

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after execution of the malware binary)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Functionality to download files from the C2 server and write them to disk.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code receives files from the C2 server and writes them to the local filesystem, enabling the attacker to deploy additional payloads or update the malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited file downloads and execution are common in malware for persistence and further compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software updates are signed and delivered through trusted channels, not arbitrary C2 servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters, but only with proper code signing and user notification.
key_indicators: Ability to write and possibly execute new files

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after execution of the malware binary)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Functionality to receive and apply configuration updates from the C2 server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code receives configuration data from the C2 server and updates its operational parameters, allowing dynamic control by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dynamic reconfiguration from a remote attacker is a common trait of advanced malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications rarely, if ever, receive silent configuration changes from untrusted remote sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise software with remote management, but with authentication and audit trails.

attack_chain.leads_to: Establishes initial connection to C2 server.

attack_chain.action: Malware establishes persistence and connects to the C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Receives commands and configuration from C2.

attack_chain.action: Malware receives and applies configuration updates from the C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Enables dynamic control of malware behavior.

attack_chain.action: Malware receives and executes shell commands from the C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote control over the system.

Malware downloads files from the C2 server and writes them to disk.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of additional payloads or updates.

behavioral_signatures: macOS process making unsolicited outbound network connections to untrusted servers
Execution of shell commands received from remote sources
File upload and download activity outside of normal user-initiated actions
Dynamic configuration updates from remote C2 infrastructure
file_indicators: Unknown Mach-O binaries with no code signing or with suspicious developer IDs
Persistence mechanisms (e.g., LaunchAgents, LaunchDaemons) referencing unknown binaries
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known SpectralBlur C2 domains or IPs
Unusual traffic patterns (e.g., encrypted C2 channels, non-standard ports)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unsigned or suspiciously signed binaries executing on macOS endpoints, especially those establishing outbound connections to untrusted IPs or domains. Detect processes that perform file uploads/downloads or execute shell commands based on remote instructions. Look for persistence artifacts (LaunchAgents/Daemons) referencing unknown binaries. Correlate network traffic with known C2 infrastructure and flag dynamic configuration updates from remote sources.
